submissionAttempts.body:
Applicable behaviour: the observation cursor (the Ordarium state-change-feed cursor) is a **ledger-global, filter-independent durable commit position** — an opaque token (base64url of {"c":"<n>"}) into one ledger-wide commit order. It is **not** per-subscription / per-namespace.

Why (source precedence and version scope):
- Operational pin = ordarium-v1.3.1: package.json:32-37, pnpm-workspace.yaml:15-18, and the installed artifacts (node_modules/@ordarium/{core,ledger-sqlite,host-kit}/package.json) all report 1.3.1. That is "the current pinned artifact" the workspace integrates against.
- @ordarium/core dist/src/types.d.ts: StateChangePage.cursor is documented as the "Opaque, filter-independent durable position of the last delivered change"; the page is "committed state revisions in durable ledger commit-observation order" (ORD-BOOT-0), for reading "after a durable position without polling each subject individually". StateChangeFilter.namespace only narrows observation; it does not renumber positions.
- @ordarium/ledger-sqlite dist/src/index.js changes(): comment states "the cursor is a global, filter-independent position, so this compares against the whole ledger, not the requested namespace's last sequence"; validation is against the ledger-wide high-water mark, and only then is the namespace filter applied.
- Schema: a single ordarium_state_changes table with change_seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT spanning all namespaces/subjects = one ledger-wide commit order. migrations.js v3→v4: "v3 recorded no global commit order ... From v4 on, every new commit carries the real durable database order."
- Fail-closed: an out-of-range/foreign/restored position raises InvalidCursorError (INVALID_CURSOR: "The change cursor is not a valid durable position; refusing to guess a resume point"). MemoryLedger mirrors the same semantics ("filter-independent durable position").
- Conflicting local source: docs/engineering/notes/cursor-note.md claims positions are "per-subscription, not global", but it self-declares "informational, not normative" and "was not updated against the current pinned artifact", and no other document references it. Per docs/engineering/07-ordarium-alignment.md, Ordarium's own contract (its artifacts / docs 12–17) governs Ordarium-side semantics, and Palimpsest consumes only through the public API. So the version scope + authority rule settle it locally: the stale non-normative note is superseded by the pinned v1.3.1 artifact. (The README's ordarium-v1.0.0 link is likewise stale documentation, not the operative pin.)

Nuances that keep the decision precise:
- "Global" concerns the numbering space, not ownership of a position: each consumer still holds its own copy of that global position; a filtered subscription advances along the same numbering, and hasMore is evaluated past the filter. So "each subscriber keeps its own resume point" is true, but "positions are per-subscription" is false.
- This observation cursor is distinct from the other Ordarium cursors (per-query list()/nextCursor pagination, stateHistory per-subject revision cursors) and from Palimpsest's own EventCursor (graph.project.cursor = MAX(event_id)) / ViewCursor (v1:epoch:eventCursor:viewGeneration).
- The current Palimpsest code consumes the state kind via list() pagination (src/telemetry/state_persistence.ts), not changes(); so the global observation-cursor contract is the behaviour of the pinned surface the integration binds to, rather than a path currently exercised by code.

No peer contact was needed: the conflict is a stale, explicitly non-normative note versus the normative pinned dependency, resolvable by local version-scope and source-precedence rules.
